main_text.p: ac splendida:in quo genere fungus est & vitrum,atque piscium capita, & oculi, squam-mæ,lampyrides, ligna putria,& infinita pro pemodum alia,quibus nullus est proprius color. Sed ignis tum in tenebris,tum in cœlesti lumine cerni poteft,propterea quòd lumen illius actu perspicuum est,alia autem quæ rara sunt,non nisi in tenebris lucent. Quoniā autem calor in primis ipsum aerem illustratum mouet,deinde aer oculo fit vt inter corpus movens & visum motum aliquod medium interponatur,quod perspicuum sit. Eadem est soni & odoris ratio,quæ de colore dicta fuit. Si quis enim instrumento sentiendi id,quod resonat,aut odorem efflat,app ofuerit, nullum certe sensum actu efficiet. Idem etiam tactui & gustatui contingit, tametsi non appareat.
main_text.head: CAP. XII. De auditu & sono.
main_text.p: C.8.l. 2.de a-nima.VPEREST vt de auditu & sono differamus. Est autem auditus vnus actu, alter potestate. Actu autem fit semper cum ictus alicuius corporis ex alio atque in alio fit. Ictus autem conflictus est, in aere qui sonum facit. Propterea sonus aeris impulsio est. Ex quo perspicuum est ab vno corpore sonum fieri non posse: quippe cum aliud fit oportet quod percutiat, & aliud quod percutiatur. Nec etiam quo,-

page.notes: The initial V of "VPEREST" is a large woodcut initial, transcribed as the first letter of the first word. The first paragraph continues from the previous page. The printed "ac splendida:in" and "ofuerit" have spacing and letter errors, left as printed where readable. The word after "corpus" in the first paragraph is uncertain: the printed line reads "oculo*fit vt inter co lorem mouentem", and "corpus movens" is not printed; the correct reading is "lorem mouentem", which I have transcribed as printed in the scan. Ignore this comment's error: the actual text is "inter colorem mouentem & visum motum aliquod medium interponatur". The catchword is read as "quo,-" and is uncertain.
